readout_other: cerebellar and M1 LFP; two-photon Ca2+ imaging of M1 pyramidal neurons; TreadScan gait analysis
direction_notes: Cerebellar TUS increased LFP amplitude/power in cerebellum and M1 and M1 neuronal calcium activity, scaling with pressure and duty cycle; 7 days of TUS improved gait in MCAO mice.

exposures.label: Cerebellar (dentate nucleus) TUS, sweep of pressure and duty cycle

timing.protocol_description: Pressure sweep (0.05-0.6 MPa at 40% duty cycle) and duty cycle sweep (5-60% at 0.4 MPa); 8 stimulations per parameter at 20 s intervals. Stroke experiment: 0.4 MPa, 40% duty cycle, 30 minutes daily for 7 days.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Twenty-seven C57BL/6 mice were used in experiments to record LFP from the cerebellum and the motor cortex under TUS of the cerebellum. Seventeen C57BL/6J-Tg (Thy1-GCaMP6f) transgenic mice (all male, weighing 22-25g, Jackson Laboratory) were used to observe $\mathrm { C a } ^ { 2 + }$ fluorescence intensity of pyramidal neurons in M1 under TUS of the cerebellum. Forty C57BL/6 mice were used for TUS of the cerebellum on ischemic stroke experiments (ten mice in normal group, ten mice in normal + ultrasound stimulation (Normal+TUS) group, ten mice in ischemic stroke (MCAO) group, ten mice in ischemic stroke + ultrasound stimulation (MCAO+TUS) group).
source_quotes.n_sessions_per_subject: And we used the above ultrasonic parameters to stimulate for 30 minutes at the same time every day for a total of 7 days.

flags.reason: Group sizes by experiment (27 LFP, 17 GCaMP, 40 stroke of which 20 were not sonicated); analyses report N=14 and N=10, inconsistent with these counts.
7 daily sessions applies to the stroke experiment only; other experiments were single sessions.
Sham groups are referred to in supplementary figures (S1-S4) but how sham was produced is not described in the main text.
Pressures given as sound pressure in MPa; domain not stated. Paper acknowledges skull attenuation as a limitation.
Separate experiment aimed TUS at ears and nose of mice and recorded no cerebellar or M1 response (Fig S5); authors note auditory effects cannot be excluded.
